description: The Subarctic Bluet is a small damselfly belonging to the Coenagrionidae family, characterized by its delicate build and predominantly blue coloration in males. Found in northern regions including parts of New England, this species is adapted to cool, northern climates and boreal habitats.

idTips.label: Abdominal Pattern
idTips.description: Males display a distinctive blue and black pattern on the abdomen with characteristic segment markings that help distinguish this species from similar bluets

idTips.label: Facial Markings
idTips.description: Look for the interrogation mark-like facial pattern (hence the scientific name 'interrogatum') on the frons and labrum

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Small damselfly, typically 28-33 mm in length, noticeably petite compared to many other damselfly species

habitat: The Subarctic Bluet inhabits cool, acidic wetlands, sphagnum bogs, and northern ponds with emergent vegetation, preferring areas with minimal pollution.
funFact: This damselfly's range extends into the Arctic and subarctic regions, making it one of the northernmost damselfly species in North America.

relatedSpecies.distinction: The taiga bluet is extremely similar to its close relative, the Subarctic Bluet, and distinguishing them often requires expert examination of specific body segments and markings.
